newsitem.title: USA: US Senate to hold nuclear waste bill vote April 8.
newsitem.headline: US Senate to hold nuclear waste bill vote April 8.

text.p: The U.S. Senate will take up a bill when it returns from Easter recess to build a temporary dump in Nevada for radioactive waste from nuclear power plants, the bill's sponsor said Friday.
Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, R-Alaska, said he filed a petition to cut off the expected filibuster by Nevada's senators to allow a vote.
In a vote scheduled for April 8, Murkowski said he expected to get the 60 votes needed to bring the bill up for final passage.
The Senate approved Murkowsi's bill last year with 63 votes, but not by the necessary 67 to override President Clinton's promised veto.
The administration again has said it would veto Murkowski's bill.
Murkowski in his statement predicted the bill would pass, but Nevada's senators have said they have enough votes to sustain a veto.

"We continue to meet with Democrat members and the administration to resolve remaining concerns," Murkowski said. "We also continue to work with Secretary (Federico) Pena and his staff at the department of Energy," he said.
"Our goal on the bill has always been to have the votes to sustain a veto, and we're confident we can do that," a spokeswoman for Nevada Democratic Sen. Richard Bryan said.

A federal court has ruled that the federal government must take control of the waste, now stored at various sites across the country, in 1998. However, the federal government will not have a long-term storage site ready for about another 15 years.
The Clinton administration opposes Murkowski's bill, saying it would prejudge Nevada as the ultimate nuclear repository and would drain resources from building a permanent facility.
